frontMatter.welcome:

Our core values – Innovation, Sustainability, and Excellence – define who we are and what we stand for. These values guide us in delivering world-class solar energy solutions, fostering an inclusive and dynamic workplace, and making a positive impact on our planet.

frontMatter.about:
Waaree Energies Limited (Group), founded in 1989, has grown to become one of the most trusted names in renewable energy, with a focus on solar power solutions. Our legacy is built on a steadfast commitment to innovation, quality, and sustainability.
With advanced manufacturing facilities and a robust global presence, we are proud to serve industries, businesses, and communities in over 68 countries. Our portfolio includes high-performance solar PV modules, energy storage systems, and turnkey EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) solutions.
Our success stems from a strong focus on environmental responsibility and technological excellence. By constantly pushing boundaries and aligning with international green energy standards, Waaree Energies Limited (Group) continues to lead the renewable energy industry into the future.
frontMatter.purpose:
This handbook is your comprehensive guide to understanding the policies, practices, and resources at Waaree Energies Limited (Group). It has been designed to help you navigate your journey with us and make the most of your experience.
- Comprehensive Information: Find detailed explanations of company policies, procedures, and benefits.
- Guidance for Success: Understand expectations and opportunities to align with the group’s vision and goals.
- Support Resources: Discover where and how to seek assistance or clarification on workplace matters.
- Read Carefully: Familiarize yourself with all sections to fully understand your rights and responsibilities.
- Reference as Needed: Use this handbook as a go-to resource for any questions about policies, entitlements, or company practices.
- Stay Updated: Note that this handbook will be updated periodically. Keep an eye out for any revisions or announcements.
If you have any queries or need additional clarification, please don’t hesitate to reach out to your manager or the Human Resources team. This handbook is a valuable tool to ensure a smooth and fulfilling career at Waaree Energies Limited (Group).
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we are committed to upholding the rights of our employees and ensuring fair labor practices across all operations. By adhering to international labor standards and local regulations, we aim to create a workplace that prioritizes respect, equality, and safety.
- No Child Labor: We do not employ anyone under 18 years old. We ensure that no one is working under the legal working age.
- Prohibition of Child Labor: We strictly adhere to the law and do not employ anyone under the age of 18. Our hiring processes ensure compliance with age verification procedures.
- No Forced Labor: Employment at Waaree

chapters.title: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Commitment
chapters.text:
Waaree Energies Limited (Group) is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that supports minority and vulnerable groups through proactive measures beyond non-discrimination.
Key actions include:
- Inclusive Communication Standards Official communications, policies, and job descriptions use gender-neutral and inclusive language.
- Physical Accessibility: Workplace facilities are designed to accommodate employees with disabilities, including ramps, accessible restrooms, and ergonomic workstations where applicable.
- All-Gender Facilities: Where feasible, gender-neutral restroom facilities are provided to ensure inclusivity and comfort for all employees.
- Flexible Work Standards: Flexible scheduling options are considered for employees with caregiving responsibilities or other vulnerable circumstances.
- Training and Awareness: Periodic sensitization and diversity awareness programs are conducted to promote respectful workplace behavior.
- Safe Reporting Channels: Confidential reporting mechanisms are available for minority or vulnerable employees to raise concerns without fear of retaliation.
- Equal Access to Development: Training and career development opportunities are made accessible to all employees regardless of background.
## Commitment to Quality, Environmental Sustainability, and Workplace Health & Safety
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we are dedicated to delivering high-quality renewable energy solutions while safeguarding the environment, health, and safety of our employees, customers, and stakeholders.
## Our Core Areas of Focus:
## Quality Commitment:
- Ensuring all products and services meet international quality standards through rigorous quality control and continuous improvement practices.
- Delivering innovative and reliable solar energy solutions to meet evolving customer needs.
- Working Parents: Groups provide resources and peer support for parents balancing professional and family responsibilities.
- Employees of Specific Gender Identities: Dedicated spaces for LGBTQ+ employees foster inclusivity, understanding, and allyship.
- Ethnic, Religious, and Cultural Groups: Forums celebrate cultural diversity, offering opportunities for employees to share their traditions and connect with others.
## Continuity and Engagement:
- These groups are supported by the organization through funding, meeting spaces, and access to resources.
- Regular events and discussions ensure these groups remain active and aligned with Waaree’s values.
## Actions to Promote the Inclusion of Employees with Disabilities
Waaree Energies Limited (Group) is dedicated to creating an inclusive environment for employees with disabilities:
## Accessible Infrastructure:
- All facilities, including entrances, workstations, restrooms, and elevators, are designed to accommodate employees with physical disabilities.
- Assistive technologies, such as screen readers or voice-to-text software, are made available for employees with visual or auditory impairments.

chapters.title: Environmental Sustainability:
chapters.text:
- Resource Optimization: Actively reducing the use of water, electricity, and raw materials through innovative technologies.
- Waste Management: Promoting recycling and safe disposal of waste materials to reduce environmental impact.
- Pollution Control: Implementing advanced pollution prevention measures and minimizing our carbon footprint.
- Eco-Friendly Practices: Using a life-cycle approach to assess the environmental impact of our products and processes.
## Health and Safety Commitment:
- Workplace Safety: Providing a hazard-free workplace through regular safety inspections, risk assessments, and the use of appropriate safety equipment.
- Health Monitoring: Conducting regular health check-ups and workplace assessments to prevent occupational illnesses.
- Safety Training: Offering mandatory safety education programs to ensure employee awareness and preparedness.
- Incident Management: Establishing clear procedures for reporting, investigating, and addressing safety incidents to prevent recurrence.
- Continuous Improvement: Regularly updating safety protocols and incorporating employee feedback to enhance workplace safety and health standards.
## Health & Safety Management for Contracted Workers
- At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), our commitment to workplace health, safety, and environmental protection extends to all individuals operating within our premises, including non-employee workers, contractors, sub-contractors, temporary staff, consultants, vendors, service providers, and third-party personnel. We ensure that consistent Occupational Health & Safety (OHS) standards are applied across all operations, regardless of employment status.
- To safeguard non-employee workers and contracted personnel, the following measures are implemented:
## Pre-Engagement Safety Controls:
- Mandatory site-specific Safety Induction before commencement of work.
- Verification of competency, certifications, and licenses for technical roles.
- Completion of Job Safety Analysis (JSA) or Risk Assessment prior to task initiation.
- Permit-to-Work authorization for high-risk activities such as electrical work, working at height, confined space entry, and hot work.
- Submission of valid medical fitness certificates for hazardous assignments.

chapters.title: Training & Awareness:
chapters.text:
- Basic Safety Awareness Training covering site hazards and emergency procedures.
- Task-specific safety training relevant to assigned duties.
- PPE usage and compliance training.
- Participation in fire safety and emergency response drills.
## Health Monitoring & Welfare:
- Periodic health check-ups for workers exposed to occupational hazards (e.g., chemicals, noise, dust, heat).
- Access to first aid and emergency medical facilities on-site.
- Safe drinking water, sanitation, and welfare facilities in compliance with statutory requirements.
## Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):
- Mandatory use of appropriate PPE at all times within operational areas.
- Regular inspections to ensure proper usage and compliance.
- Immediate corrective action for non-compliance.
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we prioritize equipping our workforce with the skills, knowledge, and resources necessary to excel in their roles. This policy provides a structured approach to identifying, planning, and executing training programs tailored to individual, departmental, and organizational needs. It also fosters a supportive environment where continuous learning and personal development are actively encouraged.
## A. Objective
The objective of the Training & Development Policy is to:
- Enhance Role-Specific Skills: Equip employees with the necessary competencies to perform their duties effectively, focusing on Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and technical proficiency.
- Promote Continuous Learning: Ensure ongoing professional growth through structured training, mentorship, and skill development programs.
- Support Workplace Excellence: Improve operational efficiency, compliance, and innovation across all functions.
- Foster Work-Life Balance and Well-Being: Provide training programs addressing repetitive strain, stress management, and family support for a healthier work environment.
## B. Scope
This policy applies to all employees, including:
- Permanent Staff: Employees working in manufacturing, quality assurance, engineering, and support functions.
- Contractual Staff: Temporary or project-based employees requiring functional training.
- New Hires and Existing Employees: Employees undergoing induction or skill enhancement programs.
## C. Roles and Responsibilities
## Training Coordinator:
- Oversees the development, execution, and tracking of training programs.
- Manages cGMP training schedules for relevant departments.
- Ensures timely delivery of on-the-job training for new hires.
- Coordinates with department heads to address training gaps.
## Department Training Coordinators:
- Identify departmental training needs, particularly around Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
- Monitor employee progress and ensure timely completion of assigned training modules.
## Subject Matter Experts (SMEs):
- Conduct training sessions, offering in-depth knowledge of their respective domains.
- Facilitate hands-on, practical learning experiences.
## Human Resources (HR):
- Organizes induction training programs for all new hires.
- Ensures seamless onboarding by aligning training content with company goals.
- Tracks training compliance and collects feedback for continuous improvement.
## Employees:
- Actively participate in training sessions and complete assigned modules within the specified timelines.
- Apply learned skills to their daily responsibilities and share feedback to enhance training effectiveness.
## D. Training Procedures
## Training Needs Identification (TNI):
- Conducted annually to assess skill gaps and align training programs with organizational objectives.
- Department heads collaborate with HR to document and address role-specific training needs.
## nduction Training:
- Purpose: Introduce new employees to the company’s mission, vision, policies, and safety protocols.
## Content:
- Overview of company operations and core values.
- Departmental orientation and role-specific responsibilities.
## cGMP and Role-Specific Training:
- Employees receive comprehensive training on cGMP standards and job-specific SOPs.
- Practical, on-the-job training is documented to ensure readiness for routine tasks.
## Continuous Professional Development (CPD):
- Programs include certifications, leadership workshops, and cross-functional training to promote career advancement.
## E. Specific Programs
## Family-Supportive Programs:
- Flexible Work Hours: Employees can tailor their schedules to better manage family obligations, promoting work-life balance.
- Parental Leave Policies: Comprehensive maternity and paternity leave policies provide adequate time off for new parents.
- Childcare Assistance: Financial support and partnerships with childcare centers to reduce childcare burdens.
- Family-Oriented Events: Organize annual family days, workshops for family well-being, and community bonding activities.

chapters.title: Emergency Preparedness & Incident Coverage:
chapters.text:
- Inclusion of contracted workers in emergency evacuation plans.
- Participation in mock drills and emergency simulations.
- Access to the same Incident Reporting Process applicable to employees.
- Clear communication channels for reporting unsafe conditions or near-miss events.
## Monitoring, Compliance & Accountability:
- Periodic contractor safety audits and site inspections.
- Tracking of contractor-related incidents, near-misses, and corrective actions.
- Integration of contractor safety performance into vendor evaluation systems.
- Enforcement of corrective measures, including warnings, suspension, or contract termination for repeated violations.
## ncident Reporting Process
- At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), safety is a priority, and ensuring that incidents are reported and addressed promptly is vital for maintaining a healthy and secure work environment. We have established a clear and effective Incident Reporting Process to identify, investigate, and resolve any safety concerns in the workplace.
- Here’s a detailed step-by-step guide for how incidents should be reported and handled:
## mmediate Reporting
- In the event of a safety incident or near-miss, the first action is to report the incident as quickly as possible.
- Report to Supervisor:
- If you experience or witness an incident, immediately notify your direct supervisor. This ensures the incident is recorded, and necessary actions are taken to address immediate risks.
- Supervisors are responsible for taking initial actions, such as stopping work to ensure safety and providing first aid if necessary.
- Alternative Reporting:
- Confidential Reporting to Safety Officer or HR:
- If you are uncomfortable reporting to your supervisor or wish to maintain confidentiality, you can contact the Safety Officer or Human Resources directly. You can reach them via:
- Email: safety@waaree.com
## Excessive Use of Force and Freedom of Movement Restrictions
## Prohibition of Excessive Force by Security Personnel:
- Security personnel employed or contracted by Waaree Energies Limited (Group) must avoid excessive force or actions that harm employees or visitors.
- Security staff receive specialized training on conflict resolution and de-escalation techniques.
- Any suspected misuse of force by security personnel must be reported immediately.

chapters.title: Freedom of Movement:
chapters.text:
- Employees have the right to move freely within their workspace, with restrictions only applied for security or operational safety reasons.
- If employees feel their movement is unfairly limited, they may file a grievance for investigation.
## Security Incident Contact Details:
## Email: security.compliance@waaree.com
## Documentation
- Proper documentation is essential to track the incident and ensure all relevant details are captured for investigation and corrective action.
- Incident Form:
- Fill out the Incident Report Form available in the HR office or online via the employee portal.
- The form should include:
- Date & Time: When the incident occurred.
- Location: Where the incident took place.
- Description: A clear and detailed account of the incident, including what happened, who was involved, and any immediate actions taken.
- Witnesses: Names and contact details of anyone who witnessed the incident.
- Submission:
- Submit the completed form to your supervisor or the HR department. The form will be logged into the Health & Safety Management System for tracking and review.
## nvestigation Process
- Once the incident has been reported, an investigation will be conducted to determine the root cause and prevent future occurrences.
- Initial Assessment:
- Safety Officer: The Safety Officer, will lead the investigation. Within 30 minutes of the report, an initial assessment will be made to determine the severity and immediate impact of the incident.
- Key factors to assess include:
- Environmental conditions at the time.
- Operational status and equipment involved.
- Eyewitness testimonies.
- Team Setup for Investigation:
- A team will be formed to conduct the detailed investigation.
- Department Head: Relevant department head (e.g., Operations, Production)
- External Experts (if needed): Technical consultants, safety experts, etc.
## nvestigation Steps
- The investigation team will follow a structured process to gather information and determine the cause of the incident.
- Witness Interviews:
- Interviews will be conducted with the involved parties and any witnesses. The HR Representative, will conduct these interviews to understand the circumstances and gather details.
- Witnesses should be interviewed within 24 hours of the incident.
- Review Surveillance Footage (if applicable):
- If available, surveillance cameras will be reviewed to provide additional context and evidence.
- Site Inspection:
- The Department Head, along with the Safety Officer, will inspect the incident site to gather physical evidence and determine contributing factors.
## Report Generation
- Once all information is gathered, the investigation team will analyze the data and compile a detailed report.
- Data Gathering:
- The Safety Officer, will collect and analyze all evidence. This includes incident forms, interviews, photographs, and any relevant data.
- Report Drafting:
- The report will include:
- The timeline of the incident.
- A detailed description of the cause and contributing factors.
- Recommendations for corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
- The report will be reviewed by senior management to ensure thoroughness.
## Management Review and Action
- Report Review:
- Senior management will review the draft report to ensure accuracy and compliance.
- Finalization: Once approved, the final report will be distributed to relevant stakeholders.
- Action Plan:
- Corrective Actions: The department head will ensure corrective actions are implemented in a timely manner.
- Tracking Progress: The actions will be tracked by the Safety Officer, with updates provided to senior management.
## Monitoring and Feedback
- Effectiveness Review:
- 30 days after corrective actions are implemented, the Safety Officer, Mr. Arvind Patel, will assess the effectiveness of the corrective actions and seek employee feedback on any improvements.
- Feedback is crucial to ensure ongoing safety improvements and prevent future incidents.
## Confidentiality and Non-Retaliation
- Confidential Reporting:
- Employees are encouraged to report incidents confidentially. Employees who wish to remain anonymous can use the anonymous reporting system via email or directly through the employee portal.
- Non-Retaliation:
- Waaree Energies Limited (Group) ensures that no employee will face retaliation or discrimination for reporting incidents. We encourage an open, transparent, and safe environment for all.
- Contact Information for Incident Reporting:
- Email: safety@waaree.com
- Human Resources Manager:
- Email: hr@waaree.com

At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we emphasize a structured, inclusive, and transparent recruitment process that ensures fairness and equal opportunities for all. Our hiring approach is designed to attract top talent, align with organizational goals, and foster a culture of excellence.

## Compensation, Benefits, and Career Path Guidelines
At Waaree Energies LTD (Group), our compensation framework and career advancement policies aim to foster a culture of fairness, reward excellence, and promote professional growth. These policies ensure that employees are fairly compensated, evaluated transparently, and provided with opportunities for meaningful career progression.
## Comprehensive Compensation Framework
1. Guiding Principles:
- Fair Wages: Employees are compensated above statutory minimum wages as per government regulations.
- Equitable Pay Practices: Pay decisions are transparent and aligned with industry standards, role responsibilities, and employee performance.
- Sustainability: Salaries are designed to balance competitiveness with the organization’s long-term sustainability.
2. Key Compensation Components:
- Base Salary: Reflects the core responsibilities and skills required for the role.
- Performance-Based Pay: Annual bonuses and incentives are tied to individual, team, and organizational achievements.
- Allowances and Statutory Benefits: Includes HRA, travel allowances, Provident Fund, and Gratuity, ensuring comprehensive financial security.
3. Market Competitiveness:
- Salaries are benchmarked annually against competitors and industry standards to ensure Waaree remains competitive in attracting and retaining top talent.
4. Determining Factors for Compensation:
- Criticality of the role to Waaree's strategic goals.
- Responsibilities, experience, and educational qualifications.
- Individual performance and competencies.
- Internal pay equity and external market trends.

chapters.title: Annual Salary Revision Policy
chapters.text:
1. Revision Timeline:
- Revisions are conducted annually and take effect on April 1st, based on performance evaluations for the previous financial year (April–March).
2. Eligibility Criteria:
- Employees who have joined on or before September 30th of the financial year are eligible for revisions in the subsequent cycle.
## Performance-Based Increments:
- Performance Ratings: Revisions are directly tied to performance appraisal ratings, which are conducted using Waaree's standardized evaluation process.
- Increment Grid: HR prepares an increment grid that categorizes percentage increases by performance levels (e.g., exceptional, meets expectations, needs improvement).
## Revision Influences:
- Individual Contributions: Measured through key performance indicators (KPIs) and 360-degree feedback.
- Team and Organizational Performance: The overall growth and profitability of Waaree impact increment percentages.
5. Non-Discriminatory Policy:
- Revisions are based on merit and exclude factors such as gender, ethnicity, caste, religion, or political affiliations.
## Bonuses, Incentives, and Recognition
## Performance Bonuses:
- Annual Bonuses: Based on the achievement of personal and organizational goals. These bonuses are reviewed during the annual appraisal cycle.
- Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): Specific KPIs tied to role responsibilities determine the bonus structure.
## Recognition Programs:
- Spot Awards: For employees demonstrating innovative solutions or exceeding expectations in their roles.
- Team Awards: For departments or teams achieving significant milestones.
## Long-Term Incentive Programs:
- Senior-level employees may participate in long-term incentive plans, aligning individual performance with the company’s long-term growth objectives.
## D. Measures to Anticipate and Minimize Layoffs
## Proactive Workforce Planning:
- Regular assessments of staffing levels and business requirements to identify potential surplus early and redeploy employees to other departments where possible.
## Upskilling and Redeployment:
- Training programs are offered to help employees acquire skills required for redeployment to different roles within the company.

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements:
chapters.text:
- Options such as reduced work hours, temporary sabbaticals, or project-based assignments are explored to avoid layoffs during economic downturns.
## Voluntary Exit Programs:
- Offering voluntary resignation schemes with financial incentives and retirement plans to reduce workforce size without involuntary layoffs.
## Employee Support in Layoff Situations:
- Advance Notice: Employees are given sufficient notice as per legal requirements and company policy.
- Financial Compensation: Severance packages based on tenure, role, and company policies are provided to support affected employees.
- Outplacement Assistance: Job search support, resume-building workshops, and career counseling services are offered.
- Priority Rehiring: Employees affected by layoffs are given priority for rehiring as roles become available.
## Wage Equality and Pay Audits
## Commitment to Equal Pay:
- Waaree is committed to ensuring equal pay for equal work, providing fairness across roles and functions regardless of gender or other personal attributes.
## Annual Pay Audits:
- HR conducts audits to identify any disparities and implement corrective measures to ensure pay equity.
- An internal wage gap analysis is performed annually and shared with senior management to maintain accountability.
## Unconscious Bias Training:
- Training programs for managers ensure that unconscious biases do not influence pay decisions.
## Employee Grievances:
- Employees can report any concerns about pay inequities confidentially via hrgrievance@waaree.com
## Compensation Adequacy
- Waaree Energies Limited (Group) is committed to providing fair and competitive compensation that reflects statutory requirements, local economic conditions, and industry standards. All employees are paid at or above the legally mandated minimum wage applicable to their location and role, with full compliance with labour laws, including overtime provisions. No unauthorized wage deductions are permitted.
- Compensation structures are reviewed annually, taking into account inflation trends, cost-of-living indices, CPI data, industry wage surveys, regional benchmarks, and internal equity considerations. Salaries are benchmarked against comparable organizations in the renewable energy and manufacturing sectors to ensure competitiveness and fairness.
- Periodic internal wage audits are conducted to promote equal pay for equal work and prevent discriminatory wage practices. Findings are reviewed by senior management, and corrective measures are implemented where necessary.
- Employees receive detailed salary statements outlining wages, allowances, overtime, and deductions, with payments made through secure bank transfers. Wage adequacy and compensation governance are reviewed annually to ensure continuous improvement and alignment with fair pay principles.
## Overtime and Work Hours Policy
## Eligibility for Overtime:
- Non-managerial employees required to work beyond their standard hours are eligible for overtime compensation.
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we understand the need for flexibility in the workplace, particularly to accommodate personal needs, family obligations, or external circumstances. Our flexible work arrangements policy ensures that employees have the flexibility to perform their duties while maintaining productivity and efficiency.
## Telecommuting (Remote Work):
- Eligibility: Employees in roles that do not require a physical presence in the office are eligible for remote work options. Employees with 3 or more months of service may apply for remote work.
- Approval Process: Requests for telecommuting must be submitted through the HR portal for approval. Supervisors will review work requirements, productivity goals, and team needs before approval is granted.
- Remote Work Expectations: Employees working remotely must ensure that:
- They are available during core hours (11:00 AM to 4:00 PM).
- Communication is maintained with the team and manager.
- Assigned tasks and KPIs are completed on time.
- Any technical support required for remote work is promptly addressed by IT.
## Compressed Work Week:
- Eligibility: Employees with approval from their Manager and HR may opt for a compressed workweek, where they work their full weekly hours in fewer than 5 days. For example, a four-day work week with extended hours on those days.
- Conditions: Employees must discuss their schedules with their department heads to ensure no disruption to workflow or team requirements.
## Flexible Hours:
- Eligibility: Employees may request flexible start and end times, subject to team approval and job requirements. The flexible hours are typically within a window of 7:30 AM to 10:00 AM for start times and 5:30 PM to 7:00 PM for end times.
- Core Hours: Employees with flexible hours must work during core business hours (11:00 AM to 4:00 PM) to ensure availability for meetings, calls, and collaboration.

chapters.title: Overtime Compensation:
chapters.text:
- Overtime is compensated at 1.5 times the standard hourly rate, ensuring fair remuneration for extra work.
## Compensatory Time-Off:
- Employees may request compensatory leave instead of overtime pay, subject to operational feasibility and approval.
## Approval Process:
- Overtime must be pre-approved by the respective HOD to qualify for compensation. Unapproved overtime is not eligible for payment.
- Exceptions may be made in critical situations, but these must be documented and justified.
## Career Development and Promotion Policy
## Merit-Based Promotions:
- Promotions are awarded based on individual performance, potential, and organizational requirements.
- Annual performance appraisals are the primary basis for promotion decisions.
## Promotion Criteria:
- High performance in achieving KPIs and exceeding role expectations.
- Feedback from supervisors and department heads.
- Demonstrated alignment with Waaree’s values and adherence to safety standards.
## Leadership Development:
- High-potential employees are identified for Leadership Development Programs, preparing them for future managerial or strategic roles.
## Promotion Timing:
- Promotions are typically evaluated during the annual appraisal cycle but may occur mid-year for exceptional performers.
## Transition Support:
- Employees promoted to new roles receive tailored training, mentorship, and onboarding to ensure a smooth transition and success in their new responsibilities.
## Equal Opportunity in Promotion and Professional Development
- Promotion decisions are based solely on documented performance evaluations, competency assessments, and business requirements.
- All eligible employees are provided equal access to training, leadership programs, and career advancement opportunities.
- HR and reporting managers are instructed to apply objective evaluation criteria and avoid bias during promotion decisions.
- Periodic reviews are conducted to monitor fairness and equal opportunity in promotions.
- Reasonable accommodations are provided to ensure accessibility for employees with disabilities in training and development programs.
## nternal Career Mobility
1. Vertical Growth:
- Employees are encouraged to advance to higher positions within their functional area. Career advancement pathways are well-defined and communicated during appraisals.
2. Horizontal Mobility:
- Cross-departmental transfers allow employees to diversify their skills and broaden their career prospects.
- Eligible employees are compensated for approved overtime at 1.5 times the standard hourly rate. Overtime details are transparently displayed in the monthly payslip and HR portal.
## D. Leave and Time-Off Integration
## Leave Balances:
- Employees can track their leave balances (annual leave, sick leave, etc.) in real-time via the HR portal.
## Leave Deductions:
- Approved leave is automatically reflected in payroll calculations, ensuring accuracy in salary adjustments for any unpaid leave.
## Transparent Approval Process:
- Leave requests and their approval status can be monitored through the portal, maintaining clear communication between employees and managers.
## E. Payroll Process
## Salary Payments:
- Salaries are processed monthly and directly credited to employees’ bank accounts on the last working day of each month.
## Payslip Details:
- Monthly payslips include a breakdown of:
- Basic salary.
- Allowances (e.g., HRA, travel).
- Bonuses and incentives.
- Deductions (e.g., taxes, Provident Fund).
- Payslips are available for download through the HR portal.
## Deductions Transparency:
- All statutory and voluntary deductions are clearly itemized on payslips, ensuring employees understand the components of their net pay.
## F. Remuneration Review and Feedback
## Annual Salary Review:
- Waaree conducts an annual review of all remuneration packages to ensure competitiveness and fairness. Salary adjustments are communicated transparently during performance evaluations and updated on the HR portal.
## Employee Feedback Mechanism:
- Employees are encouraged to share feedback on remuneration practices through surveys or direct discussions with HR. This input helps refine and improve the compensation framework.
## G. Equal Pay for Equal Work
## Commitment to Non-Discrimination:

## Waaree Group Leave Policy: A Comprehensive Guide
At Waaree Energies LTD (Group), our compensation framework and career advancement policies aim to foster a culture of fairness, reward excellence, and promote professional growth. These policies ensure that employees are fairly compensated, evaluated transparently, and provided with opportunities for meaningful career progression.
## A. Leave Types and Entitlements
## Annual Leave (Earned Leave):
## Eligibility:
- Employees are entitled to annual leave after completing six months of continuous service.
## Entitlement:
- 21 days of annual leave per calendar year.
- Accrual is calculated on a pro-rata basis, and employees can carry forward unused annual leave up to a maximum of 45 days.
## Approval Process:
- Leave applications must be submitted at least 7 days in advance and approved by the reporting manager.
## Casual Leave:
## Eligibility:
- All employees are eligible for casual leave from their first month of employment.
## Entitlement:
- 8 days of casual leave per year.
## Conditions:
- Casual leave cannot be carried forward or encashed.
- Leave requests must be made at least 2 days in advance except in emergencies.
## Sick Leave:
## Eligibility:
- Employees are entitled to paid sick leave from their first month of employment.
## Entitlement:
- 12 days of sick leave per year.
## Conditions:
- Employees are required to notify their manager on the first day of absence.
- For absences exceeding 3 consecutive days, a medical certificate must be submitted.
- Unused sick leave cannot be carried forward or encashed.

chapters.title: Maternity Leave:
chapters.text:
## Eligibility:
- Female employees who have completed at least 6 months of service before the expected delivery date are eligible.
## Entitlement:
- 26 weeks of paid leave for the first two children.
## Additional Leave:
- Female employees experiencing complications related to pregnancy, miscarriage, or medical termination are entitled to 6 additional weeks of leave on medical grounds.
## Eligibility:
- Male employees with at least 6 months of service are eligible.
## Entitlement:
- 7 days of paid leave to be taken within 2 months of childbirth.
## Special Leave (Bereavement/Marriage):
## Eligibility:
- Employees are eligible for special leave from their first month of service.
## Entitlement:
- 5 days of paid leave for the death of an immediate family member (spouse, parents, or children).
- 3 days of paid leave for the employee’s marriage.
## Compensatory Leave:
## Eligibility:
- Employees working on public holidays or rest days are eligible for compensatory leave.
## Entitlement:
- One day of leave for each day worked on a holiday or rest day, subject to managerial approval.
## B. Public Holidays
- Employees are entitled to all public holidays declared by the government of their respective work location.
- If a public holiday falls on a weekend, no compensatory leave will be provided unless work is required and pre-approved.
## C. Leave Encashment Policy
## Annual Leave Encashment:
- Employees may encash annual leave balances exceeding 45 days at the end of the calendar year.
## Encashment at Separation:
- Unused earned leave (annual leave) will be encashed at the time of resignation, retirement, or termination, calculated based on the last drawn basic salary.
## Non-Encashable Leave:
- Sick leave and casual leave cannot be encashed.
## D. Leave Application Process
## Submission:
- All leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal or via the designated leave application form.
## Approval:
- Approval is required from the immediate supervisor or reporting manager.
## Documentation:
- For sick leave exceeding 3 days, a medical certificate must be submitted within 2 days of resuming work.
- For maternity or paternity leave, a doctor’s certificate or birth certificate is required.
## E. Unplanned or Emergency Leave
- Employees must inform their reporting manager immediately if unable to report to work due to unforeseen circumstances.
- In such cases, leave will be adjusted from available casual or sick leave balances.
## F. Leave During Probation
- Employees on probation are entitled to:
- 6 days of casual leave (pro-rated).
- Sick leave on an as-needed basis, subject to approval.
## G. Leave Audits and Monitoring
## Leave Balance Updates:
- Employees can view their leave balances in real time via the HR portal.
## Monitoring and Compliance:
- HR conducts periodic leave audits to ensure compliance with policies and minimize misuse.
## Regularization of Unauthorized Absences:
- Employees with unauthorized absences must meet with their manager and HR to regularize their status.
By establishing these comprehensive leave policies, Waaree Energies Limited (Group) ensures that employees can meet their personal and professional obligations, contributing to a supportive and productive workplace.
## Attendance Recording and Working Hours Policy
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we prioritize maintaining an efficient and accountable work environment while ensuring that employees can manage their time effectively. The Attendance and Working Hours Policy is designed to balance business requirements with individual needs, providing a structure that ensures consistency and transparency in attendance management.
## A. Working Hours Policy
## Standard Working Hours:
- The standard working hours at Waaree Energies Limited (Group) are 9:30 AM to 6:30 PM, Monday to Friday, with a 1-hour lunch break from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM.
## Flexibility in Timing:
- Employees may request a flexible start time within a 1 hour window (e.g., 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM) with prior approval from their reporting manager.
- The end time must remain within the standard 9-hour working period (including breaks).
## Core Hours:
- Core working hours are from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM, during which all employees are expected to be available for meetings, collaborations, and communication.
## B. Attendance Recording
## Attendance System:
- Waaree employs an automated biometric attendance system for all employees. Employees are required to clock in and out at the beginning and end of each working day to ensure accurate recording of work hours.
- For remote work or field-based roles, attendance is tracked through the HR portal using a daily check-in/check-out system.
## Late Arrival or Early Departure:
- Employees are expected to arrive on time and adhere to their designated working hours.
- Any late arrivals or early departures must be recorded in the attendance system and justified with valid reasons (e.g., medical, family emergency).

## Employee Provident Fund (EPF) & Employee Pension Scheme (EPS)
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we prioritize the financial well-being and long-term security of our employees. As part of this commitment, we provide statutory benefits such as the Employee Provident Fund (EPF) and the Employee Pension Scheme (EPS) in compliance with the Employees' Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. These schemes ensure that employees have a secure savings foundation for their post-retirement life and unforeseen contingencies.
## A. Employee Provident Fund (EPF)
The EPF is a savings scheme designed to provide employees with financial stability during their post-employment years.
## Eligibility and Coverage:
- All employees earning a monthly basic salary of ₹15,000 or less are mandatorily covered under EPF.
- Employees earning above ₹15,000 can voluntarily opt-in for EPF contributions upon approval.
## Contribution Structure:
- Employee Contribution: Employees contribute 12% of their basic salary + dearness allowance (DA) to the EPF account.
## Employer Contribution:
- The employer matches the employee’s contribution of 12%, out of which 8.33% is directed to the EPS, and the remaining 3.67% goes to the EPF account.
## Interest and Returns:
- The EPF account earns annual interest as determined by the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).
- The interest is compounded annually and credited to the employee’s account at the end of each financial year.
## Benefits of EPF:
- Savings Growth: Contributions grow over time with compound interest.
- Partial Withdrawals: Employees can make partial withdrawals for specific purposes, such as:
- Marriage or education.
- Medical emergencies.
- Home construction or purchase.

## Records Retention and Management Framework
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we understand the importance of effective record retention and management in ensuring compliance, operational efficiency, and confidentiality. Our detailed Records Retention Framework outlines the systematic handling of all employee, third-party, and organizational records. This ensures that essential information is maintained securely, accessible when required, and disposed of responsibly after its retention period.
## A. Objective of Records Retention Framework

- Ensuring legal and regulatory compliance with applicable laws, including labor laws, tax regulations, and data protection laws.
- Supporting operational continuity through the preservation of critical records and data.

chapters.title: Grievance Resolution Procedure
chapters.text:
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we value open communication and are dedicated to maintaining a respectful and transparent work environment. Our Grievance Resolution Procedure is designed to ensure that employee concerns are addressed promptly, fairly, and systematically, thereby fostering a positive workplace culture and upholding the company's commitment to fairness, inclusivity, and accountability.
## A. Purpose
- The purpose of this procedure is to:
- Provide employees with a clear and formal mechanism to raise workplace concerns.
- Ensure grievances are handled in a timely, fair, and impartial manner.
- Promote a culture of trust, openness, and mutual respect within the organization.
- Address and resolve workplace issues before they escalate, enhancing employee satisfaction and productivity.
## B. Scope
## Applicability:
- This policy applies to all employees of Waaree Energies Limited (Group), including permanent, contractual, and temporary staff.
- Contractors, suppliers, and community members impacted by company operations are also encouraged to report concerns via designated channels.
## ssues Covered:
- Compensation and benefits discrepancies.
- Workplace harassment, discrimination, or bullying.
- Unsafe working conditions or safety violations.
- Disputes regarding policies, workloads, or treatment by supervisors.
- Ethical violations such as corruption, bribery, Child Labour, Forced labour or conflicts of interest etc.
## C. Key Benefits
The grievance resolution process provides several advantages:
- Fair and Accessible Reporting: All employees can raise concerns confidently and securely.
- Transparency: Ensures openness in the resolution process with clear communication at each step.
- Employee Engagement: Encourages employee participation in improving workplace dynamics.
- Risk Mitigation: Reduces the likelihood of legal disputes and reputational damage by addressing grievances promptly.
- Improved Culture: Strengthens a culture of respect, inclusivity, and professionalism.
## D. Definitions
- Grievance: Any concern or complaint raised by an employee related to their job, workplace environment, or company policies.
- Grievance Mechanism: A formal process that ensures grievances are systematically addressed, documented, and resolved.
## E. Reporting Methods
Employees can report grievances through multiple channels:
## HR Department:
- Contact the HR Manager directly.
- Email: hrgrievance@waaree.com
- Immediate Supervisor: Raise concerns informally or formally with the reporting manager.
- Grievance Boxes: Submit anonymous written grievances through reporting boxes placed in common areas.
- Online Reporting Portal: Use the company’s secure digital platform to submit grievances confidentially.
## Step 1: Submission of Grievance
- Employees submit their grievances formally via email, grievance form, or the online portal.
- Complaints must include a detailed description of the issue, relevant dates, parties involved, and any supporting evidence.
## Step 2: Acknowledgment of Grievance
- HR will acknowledge receipt of the grievance within one business day.
## Step 3: Preliminary Assessment
- HR conducts a preliminary review within two business days to determine if the grievance is valid and requires further investigation.
## Step 4: Investigation
- A formal investigation is initiated within 5-7 business days. This includes:
- Interviewing the complainant, respondents, and witnesses.
- Reviewing relevant documents, policies, or evidence.
- Consulting with legal or compliance experts if necessary.
## Step 5: Decision and Resolution
- The findings are evaluated, and HR or the Grievance Committee makes a decision within three business days after the investigation is concluded.
- Resolutions may include corrective actions, disciplinary measures, policy adjustments, or mediation sessions.
## Step 6: Communication of Outcome
- The complainant is informed of the resolution in writing, including any actions taken to address the grievance.
## Step 7: Appeal Process
- Employees dissatisfied with the resolution can appeal to the Grievance Redressal Committee or Senior Management within seven business days.
## G. Special Provisions
## Sensitive Grievances
- Complaints related to harassment, discrimination, or workplace violence etc. are prioritized and handled confidentially by the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC).
## Whistleblower Protections:
- Employees reporting ethical violations or misconduct are protected under the company’s Whistleblower Policy. Retaliation against complainants is strictly prohibited.
## Anonymous Complaints:
- Anonymous grievances are investigated to the extent possible while maintaining confidentiality.
## H. Record Keeping
## Documentation:
- All grievances and their resolutions are systematically documented.
## Storage:
- Records are securely stored in both physical and electronic formats, accessible only to authorized personnel.
## Preventive Measures and Training
…

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
At Waaree Energies Limited (Group), we are committed to fostering a culture of transparency, accountability, and integrity. Our Whistleblower Procedure provides a safe and confidential channel for employees and stakeholders to report unethical practices, misconduct, or violations of company policies or laws. This ensures that concerns are addressed promptly and appropriately while protecting whistleblowers from retaliation.
## A. Purpose
The purpose of the Whistleblower Procedure is to:
- Encourage employees and stakeholders to report concerns about unethical or unlawful activities.
- Provide a clear and confidential mechanism for raising concerns.
- Protect whistleblowers from any form of retaliation, ensuring they feel secure in reporting issues.
- Maintain the company’s commitment to ethical business practices and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
## B. Scope
This procedure applies to all employees, contractors, suppliers, and stakeholders associated with Waaree Energies Limited (Group) who wish to report:
- Fraud, corruption, or bribery.
- Financial irregularities or misstatements.
- Breaches of company policies, including safety violations.
- Harassment, discrimination, or workplace misconduct.
- Conflicts of interest or misuse of company resources.
- Violations of environmental, labor, or regulatory compliance.
- Other unethical or illegal practices.
## C. Key Features
- Anonymity: Whistleblowers may choose to remain anonymous when reporting concerns.
## Protection Against Retaliation:
- Retaliation against whistleblowers is strictly prohibited and may result in disciplinary action, including termination.
- Fair Investigation Process: Every report is handled impartially, ensuring a thorough and unbiased investigation.
- Confidentiality: All disclosures and investigations remain confidential to protect the whistleblower's identity and the integrity of the process.
## D. Reporting Channels
Whistleblowers can report concerns through the following channels:
## Email:
- Submit reports to whistleblower@waaree.com for direct and confidential reporting.
## Online Whistleblower Portal:
- Use the company’s secure portal to report issues anonymously through QR Code available at all the Location.
## Grievance Boxes:
- Submit written reports anonymously in designated grievance boxes available at office and factory locations.
## Direct Reporting to the Ethics Officer:
- Contact the Ethics & Compliance Officer at:
- Name: Mr. Vishal Upadhyay
## Email: Vishalupadhyay@waaree.com
## E. Reporting Process
## Submission of Report:
- Provide detailed information about the unethical activity, including:
- Nature of the concern.
- Date, time, and location of the incident.
- Names of individuals involved (if known).
- Evidence or witnesses supporting the claim.
## Acknowledgment of Report:
- Acknowledgment will be sent within two business days of receiving the report (if contact information is provided).
## Preliminary Review:
- The Ethics & Compliance Team will conduct an initial assessment within five business days to determine the validity of the report and the need for a formal investigation.
## nvestigation Process:
- If necessary, a formal investigation will be initiated, including:
- Gathering evidence and interviewing relevant parties.
- Consulting legal or external experts if required.
- Ensuring complete confidentiality during the process.
## Resolution:
- The findings and recommended actions are submitted to senior management for review and implementation.
- Whistleblowers (if identified) will be informed of the resolution and any corrective measures taken.
## Timeline:
- Investigations are typically completed within 30 days unless additional time is required due to complexity.
## F. Protection for Whistleblowers
## No Retaliation Policy:
- Any form of retaliation against whistleblowers, such as termination, demotion, harassment, or discrimination, is strictly prohibited.
- Employees who retaliate against whistleblowers will face disciplinary action, including termination.
## Support Mechanisms:
- Whistleblowers experiencing retaliation can report the matter directly to HR or the Ethics Officer for immediate redressal.
## G. Documentation and Record Keeping
## Secure Records:
- All reports, investigations, and outcomes are securely documented and stored for seven years.
## Anonymity Assurance:
- Whistleblower identities are kept confidential unless disclosure is required by law or consented to by the whistleblower.
## H. Monitoring and Feedback
## Periodic Policy Review:
- The Whistleblower Procedure is reviewed annually to ensure it remains effective and aligned with legal requirements.
## Feedback Mechanism:
- Employees can provide feedback on the whistleblower process through surveys or direct communication with HR.
## Benefits of the Whistleblower Procedure
- Reinforced Integrity: Ensures adherence to ethical practices, fostering trust among employees and stakeholders.
…
